item.title: The Gatekeeping of Jargon
item.description: Complex terminology often acts as an unintentional gatekeeper. In disciplines like machine learning and data analytics, the nomenclature can sound incredibly intimidating. Terms like “stochastic gradient descent” or “multi-head attention” sound almost mystical to an outsider. Yet, when you break them down, the core concepts, taking small steps down a hill to find the lowest point or weighing which words in a sentence relate most to each other, are intuitive. Idempotence sounds scary, but saying that pressing the elevator button 10 times for it to come down is the same as pressing it once, sounds easy. Memoization sounds harder than saying, “I write an answer on a sticky note so I do not have to do the math again.”
